text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] decode-gpu-oom detected on cluster-us-west-2 at 14:02 UTC — severity: high. Multiple streaming requests dropped. Paging oncall.

sara: @oncall here, i'm taking it — saw alerts for CUDA errors + container crashes. brief pls

mike: seeing repeated CUDA_UNSUPPORTED_EXECUTION error + kernel panic in decode nodes. logs show rapid growth in KV cache across guests.

aline: customer-success pinged: 3 customers reported request drops, one escalated. CS says they saw truncated responses and 502s.

raj: note: autoscaler recently pushed new batch of decode-v2 nodes with kernel 525.90. Might be related.

cass: +1, also telemetry shows some calls exceeding expected tokens — several requests had header max_tokens=null => fallback to model max (8k) and ran away.

sara: ok first triage: isolate node flapping, fail requests to fallback tier, enable hard cap per-request at edge. can someone run quick query on active connections per node?

mike: running now: `pgrep -a decoder && tail -n 300 /var/log/decode/runtime.log | grep -i cuda | tail -n 50`

mike: output snippet:
```
[14:00:12] cuda error: unknown execution error
[14:00:12] container restart: exit_code=137
[14:00:13] kv_cache_size=7.2GB seq=2048 req_id=abc123
[14:00:13] request max_tokens=null, user=acct-45
```

raj: looks like KV cache growth to >7GB triggers OOM on 24GB GPUs when multiple decodes concurrently. Also see a pattern where `max_tokens` header missing.

aline: CS: affected customers are prod tenants on dedicated cluster-us-west-2, two had requests failing for ~30s window.

sara: mitigation plan: (1) cordon problematic nodes (node ids: dec-05-07), (2) roll traffic to fallback smaller model `decode-1.5x` on same pool, (3) apply per-request token cap at edge 1024, (4) notify CS. Who can cordon now?

mike: i'll cordon and drain dec-05 & dec-07. `kubectl cordon dec-05 && kubectl drain dec-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

mike: done for dec-05, now dec-07.. drain in progress. logs show restart loop on dec-07.

infra-bot: dec-07 restart_count=6, last_exit=SIGKILL, host=host-ec2-7a

cass: i pushed a temporary routing rule to ramp traffic to decode-1.5x for requests with missing/invalid max_tokens header. Will monitor error rate.

sara: apply edge cap using rate-limiter: `x-max-tokens: 1024` header enforced. @raj can you confirm the gateway change?

raj: patch deployed to edge-frontend canary, rule ID rl-2026. Logs show header rewrite for requests without max_tokens.

mike: after cordon + model fallback i'm seeing decreased OOMs on remaining nodes. error rate down 70% in 3 min.

aline: CS updated customers: we applied temporary cap and routed to fallback models, working on full remediation. They asked for ETA.

sara: short ETA: stabilize next 30m, full root cause + patch in 3-6 hours. I'll confirm after post-mortem scope.

cass: quick note: adding synthetic test to catch `max_tokens=null` at ingress — creating eval to fail such requests earlier.

mike: found kernel call traces on dec-07, attaching snippet:
```
#0  0x7f3abc cudaLaunchKernel
#1  0x7f3a9b decode_step
#2  0x7f2a1a handle_request
```
Possible accelerated kernel mismatch with driver 525.90.

raj: rollback candidate: revert recent node image to driver 520.61 which was stable. But that needs a coordinated cluster restart.

sara: do we need rollback now or can we keep fallback + caps? prefer avoid mass restart while traffic already stabilizing.

mike: agree — keep fallback + caps while we gather traces. I'll collect core dumps from dec-07 before we terminate it.

infra-bot: core dump uploaded to s3://rwinf-cores/1747777777/dec-07/core.tgz

aline: CS: customer wants phone escalation if we don't have ETA within 45m. I suggested we'll provide a detailed update in 20m.

sara: assign roles: mike = runtime lead, raj = infra/driver lead, cass = routing/edge, aline = customer comms. I'll own incident lead and timeline.

mike: runtime lead update: creating reproducible load with missing max_tokens, stress test against decode-v2 on staging with driver 525.90.

mike: repro successful: aggressive prefix loop + null header triggers KV blowup in ~90s on a single session. logging PR to throttle KV growth when sequence>1024.

raj: infra: preparing node image rollback plan and a canary with driver 520.61 on dec-canary-1. holding until we confirm runtime patch viability.

cass: routing: keeping fallback in place for 60m, then gradually shift 50% back if metrics stable. setting alert if 502s > 1% for 5m.

sara: good. aline keep CS updated every 20m. mike, once runtime patch PR merges, we can deploy to canary dec-canary-1 and run the same stress repro.

mike: PR opened: `runtime: cap-kv-growth-on-null-maxtokens` — small guard before allocate. running CI now.

mike: CI passed. requested hotfix deploy to dec-canary-1.

infra-bot: hotfix deploy triggered: rollout dec-canary-1 -> dec-02 pool

mike: canary ran 10k synthetic requests with null header, no OOM observed over 15m.

raj: based on canary, driver rollback not required yet. we'll hold on full cluster changes. prepping patch notes for ops.

aline: CS: customers acknowledge temporary caps, asked for post-incident summary and what changed to prevent recurrence.

sara: after-action items (AIs):
- add ingress validation to reject missing/invalid max_tokens (cass)
- backport runtime KV cap guard to prod (mike)
- add synthetic smoke for runaway generation (raj)
- update runbook steps for driver/agent version mismatches (sara)
- CS postmortem + customer notes (aline)

cass: tagging AI done in tracker: INC-1747777

mike: patch rolled to prod pool with 5% ramp, monitoring. so far error rate steady low.

sara: ok handoff to daytime oncall in 40m. aline keep CS looped. if we see reoccurrence re-open pager.

customer-success: Customer A confirms service resumed, they saw truncated requests during the window but no data loss. Appreciative of quick patch.

sara: thanks all. i'll open incident channel for the postmortem. marking this thread as stabilized but not resolved — follow-up doc required.

incident-bot: Incident 1747777777 status: stabilized -> monitoring. Please file postmortem and link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
